story: Austin ordered security equipment for its parks and, in the same resolution, forbade its city manager from considering any camera or drone that depends upon artificial intelligence.

claims.text: The executed measure carries its resolution number and opens on a single whereas clause.
claims.quote: RESOLUTION NO. 20260812-017 WHEREAS ,
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The council states what it intends the measure to do, and the scanned text renders the word civil as eivil.
claims.quote: Austin City Council intends to invest in improving public safety and security in City parks while ensuring the protection ofeivil liberties;
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The resolution directs the city manager to write a parks security implementation plan.
claims.quote: The City Manager is directed to develop a Parks Security Implementation Plan
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The plan has to rest on an audit the parks department already had done.
claims.quote: shall use the July 2025 Parks and Recreation Department Security Audit Findings and Recommendations Report
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The resolution sets out what the plan has to establish.
claims.quote: planned operational and capital improvements, priority locations, responsible parties, funding mechanisms, and implementation timelines.
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The resolution names the equipment the city may buy.
claims.quote: The City Manager is directed to acquire, deploy, and activate equipment to improve parks security and safety, per the Security Audit, Implementation Plan, or both, potentially including but not limited to, security cameras, non-recording drones as first responders, lighting, access control/fencing/gates, signage and wayfinding, and radio communication systems.
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: Whatever the city buys has to comply with the surveillance ordinance the council adopted in April.
claims.quote: Any surveillance technology sought must be acquired, deployed, and used in full compliance with all requirements of Ordinance No. 20260423-029, codified at City Code Chapter 2-19
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The prohibition opens by forbidding the city manager from even considering such a purchase, and the sentence runs off the foot of the first page at the word artificial.
claims.quote: The City Manager shall not consider acquisition of any camera or drone system that depends upon artificial
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The prohibition finishes at the top of the second page and names what the system must not be used for.
claims.quote: intelligence to conduct surveillance or analysis.
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The resolution says which parks get the equipment first.
claims.quote: Parks with a history of violent crime shall be prioritized for the initial deployment of this equipment.
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The resolution sets the date by which the city manager owes the council committee a progress update, and the scanned text drops the space after the comma in the date.
claims.quote: The City Manager shall provide a progress update on the direction given in this Resolution to the Council Climate, Water, Environment, and Parks Committee no later than December 9,2026.
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The resolution carries its adoption date.
claims.quote: ADOPTED: August 12 , 2026
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The agenda describes the item the council took up.
claims.quote: Approve a resolution directing the City Manager to develop a security implementation plan for City parks and recreation lands and facilities
claims.source_title: Austin City Council agenda, August 12, 2026 regular meeting

claims.text: The ordinance the resolution points at requires council approval before a department may act.
claims.quote: City departments must obtain approval of the city council before
claims.source_title: Ordinance No. 20260423-029, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: Acquiring new surveillance technology is one of the acts that ordinance gates.
claims.quote: (B) acquiring new surveillance technology
claims.source_title: Ordinance No. 20260423-029, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.quote: A City department must prepare a privacy impact assessment for each surveillance technology the City department seeks to acquire
claims.source_title: Ordinance No. 20260423-029, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: That assessment has to reach the council well before the meeting where approval is sought.

claims.source_title: Ordinance No. 20260423-029, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The ordinance's own assessment treats the training of artificial intelligence as one question among several rather than as a bar.
claims.quote: including training of artificial intelligence
claims.source_title: Ordinance No. 20260423-029, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The city's published voting record holds no tally for the August meeting, because the dataset's most recent meeting predates it.
claims.source_title: City of Austin Council Voting Record, open data dataset 3c89-i35a

claims.quote: collects data in such a manner that it can be used by third parties to
claims.source_title: Ordinance No. 20260423-029, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: That numbered property names the training of artificial intelligence.
claims.quote: develop or expand products, services, or technology, including training of
claims.source_title: Ordinance No. 20260423-029, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The ordinance says what happens when one of those properties is present, and it is a weighing rather than a bar.
claims.quote: The presence of any one or more o f the factors in Subsection (C) shall weigh

claims.source_title: Ordinance No. 20260423-029, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.source_title: Ordinance No. 20260423-029, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.quote: (C) using new or existing surveillance technology, or the information it collects, for a

claims.quote: (D) entering into an agreement with a third-party entity outside o f the City to acquire,
claims.source_title: Ordinance No. 20260423-029, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.quote: must post the privacy impact assessment on a publicly
claims.source_title: Ordinance No. 20260423-029, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The ordinance's council-approval requirement is a numbered code section with its own heading, and the scanned text splits the word approval.
claims.quote: § 2-19-3 COUNCIL APPROV AL REQUIRED.
claims.source_title: Ordinance No. 20260423-029, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The privacy impact assessment is its own numbered code section, and the scanned text splits the word privacy.
claims.quote: § 2-19-4 PRIV ACY IMPACT ASSESSMENT.
claims.source_title: Ordinance No. 20260423-029, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: Subsection (C) of that section states the risk question the assessment has to determine, and the ten numbered factors run from it as one passage. The fifth of them is the one that names the training of artificial intelligence.
claims.quote: A privacy impact assessment must determine whether the surveillance technology poses more than a minimal risk to civil liberties and privacy rights, and must include at a minimum an analysis of whether the surveillance technology: (1) allows the indiscriminate collection of data without a warrant, probable cause, or reasonable suspicion of criminal activity, or a criminal nexus where the data is capable o f being associated with individuals or groups engaged in legal behavior; (2) routinely transmits sensitive personal information through data networks subject to legal or illegal access by third parties, other than networks that are completely internal to the City; (3) can store sensitive personal information in a manner allowing for broad or unrestricted sharing of or access to the information with or by third parties outside of the criminal justice system; (4) can collect sensitive personal information without a warrant, probable cause, or reasonable suspicion of criminal activity or a criminal nexus, or where the technology allows for the creation o f data records associated with particular individuals or groups; (5) collects data in such a manner that it can be used by third parties to develop or expand products, services, or technology, including training of artificial intelligence
claims.source_title: Ordinance No. 20260423-029, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.text: The resolution gives the chapter its short name, and the scanned text garbles the opening quotation mark.
claims.quote: City Code Chapter 2-19 and known as the ~' TRUST Act.
claims.source_title: Resolution No. 20260812-017, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.source_title: Ordinance No. 20260423-029, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.source_title: Ordinance No. 20260423-029, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.source_title: Ordinance No. 20260423-029, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.source_title: Ordinance No. 20260423-029, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.quote: a description of the machine learning and/or artificial intelligence capabilities and features of the surveillance technology
claims.source_title: Ordinance No. 20260423-029, City of Austin, executed copy

claims.quote: prioritized for deployment to City parks with a history of violent crimes. Approved

rejected.finding: the prohibition quoted as one contiguous sentence
rejected.reason: a page footer falls between the words artificial and intelligence in the document's text layer, so the sentence is carried as two claims rather than joined across the break

rejected.finding: a vote tally for the resolution
rejected.reason: the agenda page publishes no vote for the item and the city's own voting record dataset has loaded no meeting later than May 28th, 2026, so no tally was read on either

rejected.finding: the code library's text of City Code Chapter 2-19
rejected.reason: library.municode.com disallows this agent by name and returned 403. Not routed around. The ordinance text came from the city's own executed copy instead

rejected.finding: any statement in the resolution about artificial intelligence the city already runs, about enforcement, or about how depends upon artificial intelligence is to be judged
rejected.reason: the whole two page text was extracted and read and contains no such language. The silence is real and has no quotable string, so it is a note rather than a claim

rejected.finding: a count of the council members who sponsored the item
rejected.reason: counting them here would produce a numeral the document does not state

rejected.finding: three further artificial intelligence provisions in Section 2-19-5, the surveillance use policy
rejected.reason: A full sweep of both snapshots for the subject noun was run after an integrity judge found Section 2-19-9 in a file this run had already fetched. The resolution mentions artificial intelligence in its one clause and nowhere else. The ordinance mentions it in twelve places across five provisions. Two are carried, the assessment factor at c18 and c31 and the prohibition at c34, and one more is carried at c39. The remaining provisions require a surveillance use policy to state whether data will feed artificial intelligence tools, to state any guidelines or prohibitions on those algorithms, to state whether data is integrated with them, and to comply with the city's other technology policies. None of them changes the deck's reading and none reached a frame, so they are recorded here rather than claimed. THE POINT IS THE SWEEP, not these four. The deck's first spine was refuted by a provision six pages past the one it read, in a document it had in hand.

notes: Every quote was verified against a local extraction of the city's own PDFs made in this run, not against any third party reader.
The scanned text layer garbles the word civil as eivil in the whereas clause. The garbling is reported rather than repaired, and that clause is not set on a slide.

THE PROHIBITION IS NARROW AND MUST NOT BE OVERSTATED. It reaches a camera or drone system that depends upon artificial intelligence to conduct surveillance or analysis. It is not a ban on artificial intelligence in Austin parks or in Austin city government.
It is written against future acquisition only, in the words shall not consider acquisition.
A resolution directs a manager. It is not an ordinance and it creates no offence.
The ordinance's text layer breaks the word of as o f in several places. That garbling is the scan's and is reproduced rather than repaired, so a quote can be searched for in the source.

FIVE QUOTES WERE WIDENED IN THE PIXEL REVIEW ROUND, and none of them changed what the record says. Each had been stored cut short of words the deck legitimately printed, so a string a frame set could not be found in the claim it cited. c15, c25, c26 and c27 regained the subsection letters (A) through (D), which are in the executed copy and are what slide 5 stencils. c24 regained the words minimal risk, which slide 8 prints and which the stored quote stopped two words short of. c29, c30 and c31 are new and carry the two section headings and the risk question, so a code citation on a frame names a passage that was fetched.

c31's quote was extended through the fifth numbered factor after numeral_lint found slide 8 printing (5) with no cited claim carrying it. The position is computed by compute.py from the ordinance's own numbering, and the numeral now also appears in a quote the frame cites, which is what the lint asks for. A digit produced by a correct computation and absent from every quote is exactly the case the lint exists to surface.

c32 was added after a judge checked the caption's #TRUSTAct hashtag and found the name in the fetched resolution but in no claim. The name was correct and it was outside claim id coverage, which for a proper noun published to readers is the same defect as an unsourced numeral. The scan's garbled quotation mark is kept so the string can still be found in the document.

THE RUN'S THESIS WAS REFUTED BY A SECTION OF A DOCUMENT IT HAD ALREADY FETCHED. The deck argued that the April ordinance WEIGHED artificial intelligence as one of ten assessment factors and that the August resolution turned it into a bar. Section 2-19-9 of the same ordinance, six pages past the section the deck read, lists artificial intelligence or machine learning tools among the technologies that are NOT PERMITTED, except as consistent with City policy. c33 through c38 carry that section, the facial recognition entry beside it, and the three carve outs the chapter already contained, so the comparison the deck makes is against the whole instrument rather than against one section of it. The ordinance names artificial intelligence in five separate places and the run had read one.

c40 WAS FETCHED AFTER A JUDGE FOUND AN UNOPENED LINK ON A PAGE THIS RUN HAD ALREADY FETCHED. The agenda page names a link titled 'Actions Taken By Council' and the run's rejected list said 'the agenda page publishes no vote for the item', which was true of the page's prose and skipped the link on it. The action notes were retrieved, they record the item as Approved, and they publish no vote count, no mover and no seconder. The words vote, ayes, nays and motion appear nowhere against any item on that page. So the deck's absence sentence was right and the run had not earned it. It has now. This is the same defect as the section 2-19-9 miss, one document later, and it is the second time in one run that the answer was inside something already in hand.
